title: addato: inserting molecules into a box
purpose: Exercises `addato` [@epsrmanual], which inserts copies of molecules at random positions and orientations into an existing `.ato` box without changing its size — used e.g. to add solutes to an equilibrated solvent before an EPSR run [@soper2005]. The case covers the command-line and stdin forms and the retry branches for non-existent files.
fortran: `addato.f`: `addato` (random insertion, template-name check, merging of molecule and atom types)
system: The EPSR-test configuration (200 dimethyl sulphoxide + 400 water molecules, 3200 atoms, 300 K, cubic box 33.1213 Å) [@soperluzar1992] with 5 DMSO and 10 water molecules added (`bigbox.ato`, 615 molecules), then 4 more water (`bigbox2.ato`, 619 molecules); the box side stays 33.1213 Å, so the density rises. Positions and orientations come from the `ran1` generator state stored in the `.ato` file.
inputs: `DMSO.ato`, `WaterMolecule.ato`, `200DMSO400Water.ato` from EPSR-test. `addato 2 < addato1.stdin`: add `DMSO.ato` (name with extension) ×5 and `WaterMolecule` ×10 to `200DMSO400Water`, output `bigbox`. `addato < addato2.stdin`: number of files asked (1), a non-existent file to add (`NoFile`, retried), `WaterMolecule` ×4, a non-existent target (`NoFile2`, retried), target `bigbox.ato`, output `bigbox2`.
verification: Two program calls in one pass, the second reading the output of the first. Compared outputs: `bigbox.ato`, `bigbox2.ato`, `dirlist.txt`, all identical (header lines 615 and 619 molecules, box 0.33121300E+02 in the reference).
notes: As in the Fortran, the template of every added molecule type becomes the name of the file it was read from: the existence test opens the blank-padded `character*256` template name, which never exists. Tethered molecules are not supported by the port's reader (not used here).
